description:
Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum occupies the Carnegie Mansion in New York. Founded by Sarah and Eleanor Hewitt in 1897, it explores historical and contemporary design.

Its collections span textiles, works on paper, decorative arts, product and graphic design, wallcoverings and digital material. Objects from many periods connect the history of making with design’s role in daily life.

description:
The Walters Art Museum in Baltimore grew from the collection assembled by William and Henry Walters. Henry’s bequest to the city led to the establishment of the public museum in 1934.

Its holdings span thousands of years and many cultures, including ancient art, illuminated manuscripts, Ethiopian icons, Asian art and European painting. Historic buildings in Mount Vernon provide the setting for this varied collection.

description:
The Whitney Museum of American Art in New York was founded by Gertrude Vanderbilt Whitney in 1930 and opened in 1931. Her support for living American artists shaped its purpose.

The collection follows American art from the early twentieth century to contemporary practice, including modernism, Abstract Expressionism, Pop art and Minimalism. Its Gansevoort Street building was designed by Renzo Piano.

description:
The Canadian War Museum in Ottawa is Canada’s national museum of military history. Its origins date to 1880, and its LeBreton Flats building opened in 2005.

Collections examine armed conflict and its human consequences through vehicles, uniforms, medals, personal accounts, documents and recordings. The Beaverbrook Collection of War Art adds a substantial visual record of military experience and remembrance.

description:
The McMichael Canadian Art Collection in Kleinburg grew from the home and collection of Robert and Signe McMichael. Their interest in Tom Thomson and the Group of Seven shaped its beginnings.

Opened to the public in 1966, the institution has expanded beyond that founding gift. Its collections bring historical and contemporary Canadian artists into dialogue within a landscape setting associated with the McMichaels’ original vision.

description:
The Montreal Museum of Fine Arts brings together a wide-ranging collection of art from different cultures and historical periods. Gifts from collectors have played an important role in its development.

Quebec and Canadian art accompany international painting, contemporary art, graphic and photographic works, decorative arts and design. Collections extending from antiquity to the present connect local artistic histories with art from around the world.

description:
The Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec in Quebec City explores the history of art in Quebec. Opened in 1933, it preserves works ranging from the colonial period to contemporary practice.

Historic, modern and contemporary art form major collection areas, alongside Inuit art, decorative arts and design. Archives provide further context for the artists and artistic activity represented in the museum.

description:
The Royal Ontario Museum in Toronto opened in 1914. Its collections unite art, cultural heritage and natural history from across the world and different periods.

Artworks, cultural objects and scientific specimens support both exhibitions and research. The museum’s original heritage architecture is joined by the Michael Lee-Chin Crystal, designed by Daniel Libeskind.
